Sugarcane growth stages: from germination to maturity | ganna.in
When does tillering happen in sugarcane?
Usually around one and a half to four months after planting; it can vary with variety and season.
How many months does sugarcane take to mature?
About 10–12 months (pre-seasonal/suru) and longer for adsali (about 15–18 months); it varies with variety and region.

What matters at each stage?
Germination: even germination sets the crop stand for the whole field. If gaps appear, you have to replant.
Tillering: this is where the plant population is formed. If the early tillers survive, the chance of good canes rises.
Grand growth: demand for water and nutrition is highest at this stage.
Maturity: when the crop matures, decide irrigation and harvest timing with the local sugar factory and expert advice.

At which stage does sugarcane need the most water?
Water demand is usually highest during the grand growth stage.
What should I do if water stands in the field?
First arrange drainage, then care for the crop according to its stage; if needed, call 99787 91167 for advice with photos.
Home › Knowledge Centre › Irrigation management in sugarcane
Three stages of sugarcane are sensitive to water: germination, tillering and grand growth. Both water stress and waterlogging can cause damage.
Irrigation by stage
First irrigation: to keep moisture after planting. Note the date, because the timing of the herbicide and the drenching is linked to it.
Tillering: make sure moisture does not run short. Water stress can affect the tillers.
Grand growth: water demand is highest at this stage.
Maturity: when to cut back irrigation, as advised by the local sugar factory / expert.
If water stands in the field
First arrange drainage. Standing water can weaken the root zone. Then plan care according to the crop stage; if needed, get advice with photos.
Drip irrigation
Drip irrigation saves water and keeps moisture even. The setup and costs need to be planned in advance.
Irrigation and the Immunity Program
Sugarcane Special drenching is done after the first irrigation (or 3–4 days after herbicide) at 0.5–0.7 L / vigha. Details: Dose schedule.
Sugarcane planting seasons in Gujarat: pre-seasonal, suru, adsali
When should sugarcane be planted in Gujarat?
Usually pre-seasonal (October–November), suru (January–February) or adsali (July–August); the exact timing depends on the region and variety.
Why note the date of the first irrigation for drenching?
Because the advice is to do the Sugarcane Special drenching after the first irrigation (or 3–4 days after herbicide).

Common sugarcane problems: symptoms and causes | ganna.in
Why do sugarcane leaves turn yellow?
There can be many causes, such as water stress or waterlogging, nutrient deficiency or pests; first check moisture and drainage, then get advice with photos.
What information is needed for advice?
Photos, variety, planting date, current stage, irrigation and the fertilizers/sprays applied so far.
